papers.title: MobileSleepNet: A Deployment-Oriented Framework for Sleep Staging on Mobile Devices.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper presents MobileSleepNet, an ultra-lightweight framework for on-device sleep staging using single-channel EEG, designed for mobile hardware with a compact convolutional backbone and a neural-parameter-free hybrid temporal refinement strategy. Evaluations on four public PSG datasets show accuracy comparable to much larger models, with low latency and energy consumption on mobile processors.

papers.title: A single-channel EEG classification system for multiscale characterization of mouse vigilance state
papers.summary: Developed a single-channel EEG-only framework for cross-animal sleep staging in mice, using a convolutional-recurrent classifier with causal temporal smoothing and hypnodensity analysis. Achieved 0.897 accuracy and 0.856 macro-F1 across unseen animals, preserving sleep architecture and enabling long-term analysis.

papers.title: Calibration-free Plug-and-Play EEG-based BCIs.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence
papers.summary: The paper proposes Local Online Transfer Learning (LOTL), an online transfer learning method for calibration-free EEG-based BCIs that enables immediate response without subject-specific calibration. Theoretical guarantees and experiments on four EEG datasets demonstrate its effectiveness, suggesting potential for real-world BCI deployment.

papers.title: A novel algorithm integrating multimodal information for improving OSA-related sleep staging.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a dual-branch, multimodal neural network integrating SpO2-derived OSA-related information to improve sleep staging accuracy for OSA patients. Across over 1.45 million samples from three datasets, the model achieved increments of 0.18% in ACC, 1.14% in MF1, and 0.006 in Kappa for severe OSA patients compared to a model without the OSA enhancement.

papers.title: Seizure detection using hierarchical temporal trend integration and self-supervised learning.
papers.summary: The paper proposes Federated Temporal Learning (FTL), a framework combining a supervised seizure classifier with a self-supervised temporal sequence consistency task, using Hierarchical Temporal Trend Integration Modules (HTTIMs) for multi-scale EEG feature extraction. It reports state-of-the-art performance on TUSZ and Zenodo NICU EEG datasets, with high accuracy and F1 scores, and provides a theoretical stability bound.

papers.title: OOD Detection for EEG-based Machine Learning in High-Risk Environments
papers.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in EEG-based machine learning for high-risk settings, evaluating various OOD detection and uncertainty estimation methods and their impact on two clinical downstream tasks. The results disentangle OOD detection from uncertainty estimation and show how combining complementary methods can create a robust safety net for real-world EEG model deployment.

papers.title: Investigating the Influence of Anti-Seizure Medications on Aperiodic EEG Activity
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of lamotrigine and levetiracetam on aperiodic and periodic EEG activity in healthy volunteers. Results show that lamotrigine reduced aperiodic offset and exponent during eyes-open, while levetiracetam reduced exponent only, and both drugs altered periodic power in specific bands, suggesting aperiodic measures may reflect ASM neurophysiological effects.

papers.title: Dataset distillation for efficient seizure prediction: tiny-scale data, comparable performance.
papers.summary: This study presents the first dataset distillation method for EEG-based seizure prediction, condensing data into a tiny synthetic set that retains performance. Using 1% of the original data, the approach retained ~95% of the original performance while reducing training time by ~98%, validated across 72 subjects and various model architectures.

papers.title: Delta2Gamma: Band-Wise Adaptive Contrastive Learning of EEG for Alzheimer's Disease Detection
papers.summary: This paper introduces Delta2Gamma, a self-supervised contrastive learning framework for EEG that decomposes signals into five canonical bands, each with its own encoder and adaptive temperature. On the ADFTD cohort under leave-one-subject-out, it achieved 92.4% accuracy in detecting Alzheimer's disease, surpassing supervised backbones and dedicated EEG methods.

papers.title: An EEG-based non-linear state-space model for trust inference in a space-relevant human-autonomy teaming task.
papers.summary: The paper presents an EEG-based non-linear state-space model for continuous trust inference in human-autonomy teaming during a space-relevant supervisory task. The model achieved significantly higher correlation with self-reported trust than linear dynamic and static models, and revealed that trust inference relies on distributed neural features from frontal and prefrontal regions in delta, alpha, and gamma bands.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Benchmark of EEG-Based BCI Deep Learning Models for MCI and Dementia Classification
papers.summary: This study benchmarks ten deep learning models for EEG-based MCI and dementia classification across four datasets and eight tasks using a unified pipeline. SCCNet achieved the highest subject-level accuracy, while ShallowConvNet led in segment-level metrics, and performance varied across datasets, with compact models remaining competitive.

papers.title: Enhancing Motor Imagery Decoding for Stroke Patients Using Data Augmentation and Transfer Learning.
papers.summary: The paper introduces WalkBCI, a real-time motor imagery BCI system for stroke patients that integrates generative adversarial networks and transfer learning to reduce calibration time and improve decoding accuracy. In offline experiments, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score increased by up to 3.8%, while online experiments showed stable performance with up to 72.5% accuracy and 58% reduction in calibration time.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Scalp-Level Nonlinear Source Separation in Electroencephalogram: A Comparative Evaluation of Spatiotemporal Architectures.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: This study evaluates deep learning architectures for nonlinear source separation in EEG, comparing tree-based forests, CNN, LSTM, Transformer, and CNN-LSTM on synthetic and experimental ERP datasets. CNN-LSTM combined models achieved superior signal reconstruction and anatomical localization accuracy, highlighting their potential for separating nonlinearly mixed ERPs.

papers.title: A first realization of reinforcement learning-based closed-loop EEG-TMS.
papers.summary: This paper reports the first realization of a reinforcement learning-based closed-loop EEG-TMS system that identifies the μ-rhythm phase associated with high vs. low corticospinal excitability in 25 participants. Reinforced stimulation induced long-term increases vs. decreases in functional connectivity, demonstrating feasibility of user-independent adaptive brain state-dependent stimulation.

papers.title: Prospective validation protocol for artificial intelligence-assisted standardization of Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores using electroencephalography and clinical data in disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a prospective validation study of an AI system that standardizes Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) scores by integrating EEG and clinical data in disorders of consciousness. The primary endpoint is reduction in absolute CRS-R total-score error with AI assistance compared to an adjudicated reference.

papers.title: Contrastive Learning with Variational Regularization for Multi-Session EEG-to-Speech Decoding
papers.summary: This paper presents a contrastive learning method with variational regularization for EEG-to-speech decoding that leverages repeated EEG responses across sessions as positive pairs. Combining session-invariant contrastive learning with variational regularization improved character error rate while maintaining mel-spectrogram fidelity and achieved session-invariance in encoder representations.

papers.title: Altered early cortical EEG maturation and its relationship to language development in Down syndrome
papers.summary: This study analyzed longitudinal resting-state EEG from children with Down syndrome and typically developing children, finding altered maturation of aperiodic and periodic spectral features in Down syndrome. In Down syndrome, a spectral dimension was associated with verbal developmental quotient rather than chronological age, indicating altered relationship between cortical organization and language development.

papers.title: Multiscale entropy is related to iron status in resting state EEG data
papers.summary: This study applied multiscale entropy (MSE) analysis to resting-state EEG data from women with iron deficiency without anemia (IDNA) and iron-sufficient (IS) controls. The IS group showed higher overall entropy, particularly at longer time scales and frontal/parietal electrodes, suggesting IDNA may impair long-distance brain interactions.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Resting State Quantitative EEG and Daytime Sleepiness Complaints in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: In 62 Parkinson's disease participants, resting-state qEEG after awakening was related to daytime sleepiness severity (Epworth Sleepiness Scale). Lower occipital low-alpha phase synchrony was the best predictor of higher sleepiness, suggesting disrupted arousal networks contribute to daytime sleepiness in PD.

papers.title: Quantitative electroencephalography as a next-generation tool in neurodiagnostics: significance, clinical applications, and practical interpretative frameworks.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the methodology, clinical applications, and interpretative frameworks of quantitative electroencephalography (QEEG) in neurodiagnostics. It reports QEEG's potential in identifying electrophysiological subtypes in ADHD and ASD, providing biomarkers in affective and anxiety disorders, and aiding personalization of neuromodulatory therapies.

papers.title: Seizure Onset Zone Localization in Drug-Resistant Epilepsy Using Self-Supervised Learning on Stereo-EEG
papers.summary: Developed CSOPE-Net, a self-supervised CNN-Transformer encoder for seizure onset zone (SOZ) localization from stereo-EEG. Achieved ROC-AUC 0.854 in cross-validation, 0.935 on held-out good-outcome subjects, and 0.822 on external cohort, also identifying SOZ-like contacts in poor-outcome patients.

papers.title: EEG-based brain-computer interface (BCI) dataset for directional word recognition.
papers.summary: This dataset paper describes an EEG dataset recorded from 22 healthy volunteers during overt and covert articulation of six spatial-direction words, including 38 EEG electrodes and simultaneous EMG in a subset. Standard classifiers achieved up to 78% accuracy in distinguishing conditions, supporting development of inner speech recognition for brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title: Patient-Specific Non-Invasive Epileptogenic Zone Localization via High-Resolution Time-Frequency Representations and CNN Deep Learning.
papers.summary: Developed an automated non-invasive epileptogenic zone (EZ) localization framework integrating scalp EEG source imaging, high-resolution time-frequency analysis, and deep learning. The ResNet18-Superlet combination achieved 81.15% accuracy and 84.82% AUC in the adult cohort, outperforming HFO-based methods and generalizing to pediatric cohorts.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG microstate dynamics indicate altered brain network temporal organization in age-related hearing loss.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG microstate dynamics were compared between older adults with age-related hearing loss and normal-hearing controls, revealing altered transition probabilities among sensorimotor and higher-order cognitive networks that correlated with hearing thresholds.

papers.title: Clinical EEG In Modern Psychiatry: Diagnostics and Prediction.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the role of clinical EEG in psychiatry, highlighting its use in detecting epileptiform activity, excluding organic brain dysfunction, and monitoring treatments. It reports growing evidence that quantitative EEG features, particularly in depression, have small-to-moderate predictive effects for treatment responses, potentially improving outcomes at the population level.

papers.title: Conditional Spatial Classification of Expert-Confirmed Interictal Epileptiform Discharge Epochs: An EEG-ECG Ablation and SHAP Analysis
papers.summary: This study evaluated conditional spatial classification of expert-confirmed interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) epochs using machine learning and SHAP analysis. Including ECG channels improved classification accuracy (CatBoost: 93.25% with EEG+ECG vs 88.89% EEG-only LDA), with ECG-derived features contributing to model predictions, but not establishing physiological biomarkers.

papers.title: Automating Learner Assessment: Benchmarking Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for EEG-Based Familiarity Prediction
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 15 machine learning and deep learning models for EEG-based familiarity prediction, demonstrating that trial-independent validation reduces performance from near perfect to 0.6038 F1-score, and identifies gamma and beta oscillations as key biomarkers.

papers.title: Early Ictal Dynamics in Childhood Absence Epilepsy: Scalp EEG Detection of Direct Current Shifts and High-Frequency Oscillations.
papers.summary: This case report of two pediatric patients with childhood absence epilepsy describes scalp wide-band EEG capturing ictal DC shifts and high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) during seizures. A reproducible temporal sequence was observed: negative DC shifts emerged before the first spike-and-wave complex, followed by spike-locked HFOs, suggesting potential early ictal biomarkers.

papers.title: Predicting big five personality traits from resting-state EEG connectivity: a connectome predictive modeling study.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG connectivity using connectome predictive modeling modestly predicted Big Five traits (conscientiousness, extraversion, neuroticism) in a student sample, but only neuroticism survived multiple comparison correction, emphasizing the need for replication.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of central and peripheral processes in novel word acquisition: Evidence from co-registration of EEG and kinematics in natural handwriting.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
papers.summary: This study combined EEG and handwriting kinematics in 63 native Spanish speakers to track novel word learning across repeated handwritten production, finding that central orthographic encoding reaches an asymptote after four exposures while motor refinement follows a protracted trajectory, and that neural modulation during learning predicts subsequent lexical competition after consolidation. The results indicate cascaded coordination between central and peripheral processes, with the motor system operating on partially specified linguistic information to establish word-level orthographic representations.

papers.title: Auditory attention improves scale-invariant neural fidelity to speech across three EEG datasets
papers.summary: The study tested whether auditory attention improves scale-invariant neural fidelity to speech, using a leakage-resistant analysis across three EEG datasets (52 participants). They found higher fidelity for attended speech, replicating across validation samples, and demonstrated that selective attention is evident in scale-invariant preservation of target dynamics.

papers.title: Early infantile developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: clinical spectrum, diagnosis, outcomes, and evolving treatment strategies.
keywords: early infantile developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes the clinical spectrum, diagnosis, outcomes, and evolving treatment strategies for early infantile developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (EIDEE), noting that genetic diagnosis yields 60-65% with common causes including STXBP1, KCNQ2, and SCN2A variants. Outcomes are generally poor and etiology-dependent, with mortality reaching 25% in genetic cohorts, while genotype-guided therapies such as sodium channel blockers and emerging antisense oligonucleotides represent advances.

papers.title: Spectral analysis of hard-constraint PINNs: The spatial modulation mechanism of boundary functions.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
papers.summary: This paper establishes a Neural Tangent Kernel framework for hard-constraint physics-informed neural networks (HC-PINNs), showing that the boundary function acts as a spatial modulator of the kernel eigenspectrum. The effective rank is identified as a robust predictor of training convergence, and an automated boundary function design algorithm is proposed and validated on multiple PDE benchmarks.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation, Decision Fatigue, and Clinical Performance in Medical Training: A Narrative Review and Perspective on Neurophysiological Monitoring.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on how sleep deprivation and decision fatigue impair clinical performance in medical training and discusses EEG and fNIRS as candidate monitoring tools. It proposes the CBME-BCI-Fatigue framework as a hypothesis-generating model for integrating physiological state with competency-based assessment, emphasizing that real-time neurophysiological monitoring for readiness assessment remains conceptual.

papers.title: SEEG Contact Detector: A 3D Slicer Extension for Automated Localisation of Intracranial Electrode Contacts
papers.summary: The paper presents an open-source 3D Slicer extension for automated localization of intracranial electrode contacts, combining anchor bolt-based initialization, probabilistic segmentation, and non-linear modeling. Evaluated on 78 cases with 1,078 electrodes, it achieved high accuracy (median deviation 0.10 mm) and required manual correction in only 0.65% of electrodes.

papers.title: Behavioral Electrophysiology in Manduca Sexta: The Explore/Exploit Framework.
papers.summary: The paper proposes an 'Explore/Exploit framework' for neuroethology, combining frugal 'Exploratory Tools' with high-end devices, and demonstrates it with simultaneous neural recordings and flapping force measurements in Manduca sexta using a low-cost force transducer. This hybrid approach helped assess experimental challenges and test innovations.

papers.title: Compared with What? A Missing Comparator for Continuous EEG after Ischemic Stroke.
papers.summary: This letter discusses a missing comparator in continuous EEG studies after ischemic stroke, highlighting methodological concerns.

papers.title: Involvement of SIRT3 downstream targets ANT1, VDAC, CYPD, and Drp1 in a rat model of hepatic encephalopathy: Therapeutic role of thymoquinone.
papers.journal: Iranian journal of basic medical sciences
papers.summary: This study in a rat model of hepatic encephalopathy (HE) found that thymoquinone treatment increased mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced oxidative stress, and reversed HE-induced changes in SIRT3 downstream targets (ANT1, VDAC, CYPD, Drp1). Thymoquinone also increased EEG power in the dentate gyrus, suggesting activation of AMPK/PGC-1α/SIRT3 signaling.

papers.title: Reply to "Compared with What? A Missing Comparator for Continuous EEG after Ischemic Stroke".
papers.summary: This letter is a reply to the commentary about a missing comparator in continuous EEG after ischemic stroke, providing authors' response.

papers.title: The application of traditional machine learning and deep learning with EEG for mild cognitive impairment: a bibliometric analysis.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis of 547 studies maps the field of EEG and machine learning in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), showing rapid post-2018 growth, China's leading publication count, and a shift from traditional feature engineering to deep learning and multimodal fusion. Frontier topics include feature selection, decision trees, and neuropsychological assessment combined with EEG indicators.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
